# Plugin content modules

Use this skill for one of three tasks:

- [Create a new content module](#create-a-new-content-module).
- [Convert an existing module](#convert-an-existing-module) that the build merges into the plugin descriptor module.
- [Extract an optional dependency](#extract-an-optional-dependency) of a module into a new content module.

This skill does not apply to a module in the core plugin (`com.intellij`).
The core plugin registers its content modules in a module set. See the [Product DSL](../../../platform/build-scripts/product-dsl/README.md).

The rules live in the docs. Read them, and do not restate them in code or in other skills:

- [Creating a plugin content module](../../../../docs/IntelliJ-Platform/4_man/Plugin-Model/Creating-content-module.md): the descriptor, the visibility, the registration and the compatibility.
- [Modules in project sources](../../../../docs/IntelliJ-Platform/4_man/Modularization/1_Modules-in-project-sources.md): the source roots and the package prefix.
- [Plugin Model v1 and v2](../../../../docs/IntelliJ-Platform/4_man/Plugin-Model/Plugin-Model-v1-v2.md#plugin-content-module): the loading rules.
- [Plugin directory structure](../../../../docs/IntelliJ-Platform/4_man/Remote-Development/Modular%20Plugin%20Architecture/1_Plugin-Directory-Structure.md): the layout of a split mode plugin.

Other skills cover nearby tasks:

- To change `.iml` dependencies, use the `module-dependencies` skill.
- To query which plugins and products include a module, use the `plugin-model-analyzer` skill.
- To split a plugin for split mode, use the `remote-dev` skill.

## Create a new content module

Create the module with the CLI. Do not write an `.iml` or a `modules.xml` entry by hand:

```bash
bun build/jps-module.mjs create <module-dir>/<module-name>.iml [--kind empty|shared|frontend|backend] [--plugin <plugin.xml>]
```

The command does these steps:

- It writes the `.iml` in the canonical form. The `src` root gets the root package `com.<module-name>` as its package prefix.
- The kinds `shared`, `frontend` and `backend` copy the template `plugins/.remdev/remDevFeatureSample.<kind>`. Only the ultimate checkout has the template.
- It registers the module in `.idea/modules.xml`, and also in `community/.idea/modules.xml` for a community module.
- It adds `<module name="..."/>` to the `<content>` of the plugin descriptor, with the loading rule of the kind.

Rules for the arguments:

- The name of the `.iml` file is the module name. Its directory is the module directory. Each module needs a directory of its own.
- The default kind is the suffix of the module name: `.shared`, `.frontend` or `.backend`. Any other name gets `empty`.
- Create the `.shared` module first. A `frontend` or `backend` module refuses to start without it.
- For `shared`, `frontend` and `backend`, the default plugin descriptor is `../resources/META-INF/plugin.xml` beside the module directory. Pass `--plugin` for another descriptor.
- An `empty` module goes into a plugin only with `--plugin`, because a test or helper module is not a content module.
- An `empty` module gets no loading rule, so it is `optional`. Add `loading="required"` to its entry when the plugin needs it.

The templates declare `kotlin-stdlib` and the `.shared` module with `scope="RUNTIME"`.
When the code of the module uses them at compile time, change the scope with the `module-dependencies` skill.
Without `kotlin-stdlib` at compile time, Kotlin fails with `Cannot access built-in declaration 'kotlin.Any'` on almost every line.

Then do the [common steps](#common-steps).

The package prefix keeps the source tree flat. The file `com/intellij/foo/bar/Baz.kt` of the module `intellij.foo` goes to `src/bar/Baz.kt`.
A package outside `com.<module-name>` fails `IntelliJProjectPackageNamesTest`.

## Convert an existing module

Use this when a JPS module already exists and the build merges it into the plugin descriptor module.
The goal is to register it as a content module and keep the same behavior at runtime.

### 1. Find how the plugin includes the module now

Search for the module name and for the file name of its XML descriptor.
Record the current form. It sets the loading rule in step 3.

| Current form | Loading rule |
| --- | --- |
| `<depends optional="true" config-file="...">` in `plugin.xml` | `optional` (the default, no attribute) |
| `<xi:include>` with an empty `<xi:fallback/>` | `optional` |
| `<xi:include>` without a fallback | `required` |
| A JAR in a subdirectory of `lib`, so the IDE process does not load it | `on-demand` |
| The JAR is in the plugin, but the module has no XML of its own | `required` |

Also find where the build layout names the module:

- `pluginAuto(...)` `moduleNames` or `spec.withModule(...)` in `CommunityRepositoryModules.kt` or `UltimateRepositoryModules.kt`.
- An automatic merge by `inferModuleSources` in `autoLayout.kt`, when the module name starts with the plugin descriptor module name.

### 2. Move the module descriptor

Put the descriptor at `<module-dir>/resources/<module-name>.xml`. Do not put it in `META-INF`.
If the old XML is in `META-INF` or has a different name, move it with `git mv`.
The docs list the tags that a module descriptor can have.
Remove the `package` attribute. Keep a `<module value="..."/>` plugin alias only when the old code already declared it.

### 3. Register the module in the plugin descriptor

Add the module to the `<content>` of the plugin `plugin.xml`, with the loading rule from step 1.
Remove the old `depends` or `xi:include` tag.
Remove the module from the build layout entries that you found in step 1. The build adds a content module to the distribution automatically.

If the layout gave the JAR a custom name, update the code that uses that name.
A content module goes to `lib/<module-name>.jar` when it is embedded, and to `lib/modules/<module-name>.jar` in the other cases.
When the layout spec becomes empty, remove the whole `pluginAuto` or `plugin` call.

### 4. Keep compatibility with external plugins

Skip this step for `loading="embedded"`.
Call the `get_external_usage_statistics` tool for each public class. The index covers only Marketplace plugins, so an empty result does not prove safety.
If there are external usages, call `find_external_usages` on `plugin.xml` to see how the external plugins depend on the plugin.

Then do the [common steps](#common-steps).

## Extract an optional dependency

Use this to make a dependency X of a host module optional: move the code that uses X into a new content module.
The host module works when the new module is absent, and behaves the same when it is present.

### Choose the pattern

- **Pattern A, a simple move.** The code that uses X is in a few files, and the host module does not call them. Move these files to the new module.
- **Pattern B, an extension point.** The core files of the host module refer to X in many places. Declare an extension point in the host module without X imports. Implement it in the new module, and replace each direct X call with a null-safe static helper.

### 1. Create the module

[Create the module](#create-a-new-content-module) with `bun build/jps-module.mjs create <module-dir>/<module-name>.iml --plugin <plugin.xml>`.
The kind is usually `empty`, which makes it `optional`.
Add its dependencies with the `module-dependencies` skill: the host module and X.

### 2. Move the code

- Keep the type of a moved file, Kotlin or Java. Write new code in Kotlin.
- Move the file and change its `package` declaration together.
- Keep the availability in IDEA Free mode. The host module and the new module both keep the availability of the original module. `PluginsAvailableInIdeaFreeModeTest` checks this.

Bazel strict deps needs a direct `.iml` dependency for each class that the code uses. These classes live in modules that their package names do not suggest:

| Class(es) | Package | `.iml` module | Bazel target |
|-----------|---------|---------------|--------------|
| `ExecutionException`, `GeneralCommandLine`, `KillableColoredProcessHandler`, `OSProcessHandler`, `ScriptRunnerUtil`, `Url`, `NetUtils` | `com.intellij.execution.*`, `com.intellij.util.*` | `intellij.platform.ide.util.io` | `@community//platform/platform-util-io:ide-util-io` |
| `AsyncPromise`, `Promise` | `org.jetbrains.concurrency` | `intellij.platform.concurrency` | `@community//platform/util/concurrency` |
| `AppExecutorUtil`, `ProcessAdapter`, `ProcessEvent`, `ProcessOutputTypes`, `ParametersListUtil`, `FileUtil`, `StringUtil` | `com.intellij.util.*`, `com.intellij.openapi.util.*` | `intellij.platform.util` | `@community//platform/util` |
| `Editor` | `com.intellij.openapi.editor` | `intellij.platform.editor.ui` | `@community//platform/editor-ui-api` |
| `MultipleLangCommentProvider` | `com.intellij.psi.templateLanguages` | `intellij.platform.lang.impl` | `@community//platform/lang-impl` |

When the code calls a method whose return type comes from a third module, that module is also a direct dependency. Kotlin checks the return type at compile time.

### 3. Declare the extension point (Pattern B only)

Declare the extension point in the descriptor of the host module with `qualifiedName`:

```xml
<extensionPoints>
  <extensionPoint qualifiedName="com.intellij.<language>.<epName>"
                  interface="com.intellij.<language>.<feature>.MyFeatureHelper"
                  dynamic="true"/>
</extensionPoints>
```

Write the interface in the host module, without X imports. Give it `@JvmStatic` helpers that return a no-op result when no extension is registered:

```kotlin
interface MyFeatureHelper {
  fun doSomething(element: PsiElement): Boolean

  companion object {
    @JvmField
    val EP = ExtensionPointName.create<MyFeatureHelper>("com.intellij.<language>.<epName>")

    // An extension point can have several extensions. Process all of them.
    @JvmStatic fun checkSomething(element: PsiElement?): Boolean =
      element != null && EP.extensionList.any { it.doSomething(element) }
  }
}
```

Register the implementation in the descriptor of the new module:

```xml
<extensions defaultExtensionNs="com.intellij">
  <<language>.<epName> implementation="com.intellij.<language>.<feature>.MyFeatureHelperImpl"/>
</extensions>
```

When the operations of X form a lifecycle, put them in one extension point, not one per method.
When a step passes state of an X type to a later step, type the state as `Any?` in the interface. The implementation casts it back:

```kotlin
// In the host module, without X imports
interface MyLifecycleHelper {
  fun captureState(file: PsiFile): Any?
  fun applyState(file: PsiFile, state: Any?)
}

// In the new module
internal class MyLifecycleHelperImpl : MyLifecycleHelper {
  override fun captureState(file: PsiFile): Any? = getThings(file)

  override fun applyState(file: PsiFile, state: Any?) {
    @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
    val things = state as? List<XThing> ?: emptyList()
  }
}
```

### 4. Fix the users of the removed dependency

A module that used X through the host module can break. `AllProductsPackagingTest#targetValidations` names it.
Add the dependency to its descriptor before the `<!-- region Generated dependencies -->` marker, inside the same `<dependencies>` tag:

```xml
<dependencies>
  <module name="intellij.some.formerly.transitive.module"/>
  <!-- region Generated dependencies - run `Generate Product Layouts` to regenerate -->
  ...
  <!-- endregion -->
</dependencies>
```

Do not add a second `<dependencies>` tag. `AllProductsPackagingTest#suiteValidations` then reports the file as out of sync.

When another plugin uses a moved class, do these steps for that plugin:

1. Add `<module name="intellij.new.module"/>` to its descriptor.
2. Add the module to its `.iml` with the `module-dependencies` skill.
3. Set the visibility of the new module. The docs say which level to use.

Kotlin classes are `final` by default. When another module subclasses a moved class or its inner class, mark both classes `open`.
Otherwise the other module fails with `cannot inherit from final class`.

Then do the [common steps](#common-steps).

## Common steps

1. Run `./build/jpsModelToBazel.cmd` after an `.iml` change. In a community checkout, run `./build/jpsModelToBazelCommunityOnly.cmd`.
2. Run `./bazel.cmd run //platform/buildScripts:plugin-model-tool`. It generates the `<dependencies>` of the module descriptors from the `.iml` files. Read each change that it makes.
3. Run `./community/tools/bt.cmd build` for the new module and for each module whose descriptor changed.
4. Run the tests. `bt` refuses `intellij.projectStructureTests`, because its tests do not run under Bazel yet, so these tests use `tests.cmd`.
   Run the `tests.cmd` runs one at a time. Each run stops the `ide-tests` processes of a run that is still in progress.

```bash
./community/tools/bt.cmd //build/tests/smoke:all-products-packaging_test
./tests.cmd --module intellij.projectStructureTests --test com.intellij.ideaProjectStructure.fast.IntelliJProjectPackageNamesTest
./tests.cmd --module intellij.projectStructureTests --test com.intellij.ideaProjectStructure.fast.PluginsAvailableInIdeaFreeModeTest
```

For Rider, also run `./tests.cmd --module intellij.rider.build.tests --test com.jetbrains.rider.build.RiderPackagingTest` from the ultimate root. After a conversion, search for the old descriptor file name. No `xi:include` or `config-file` reference to it can remain.

## Pitfalls

| Pitfall | Symptom | Fix |
|---------|---------|-----|
| A `src` tree that repeats the root package as directories | Deep `src/com/intellij/...` folders | Keep the package prefix of `src`, and move the files up |
| A package outside `com.<module-name>` | `IntelliJProjectPackageNamesTest` fails | Rename the package. Do not add an entry to `non-standard-root-packages.txt` for a new module |
| A moved file with the old `package` declaration | `IntelliJProjectPackageNamesTest`: "packages [com.old.pkg] are found in the module" | Change the `package` declaration with the move |
| An extension point with `name` instead of `qualifiedName` | The extension point is not found | Use `qualifiedName="com.intellij.<language>.<epName>"` |
| A skipped `plugin-model-tool` run | The generated descriptors have stale dependencies | Run `./bazel.cmd run //platform/buildScripts:plugin-model-tool` |
| A supertype in a removed dependency | `Cannot access 'com.X.BaseClass' which is a supertype of 'SubClass'` | Kotlin needs the full supertype chain of each used type. Move the use of `SubClass` into the extension point implementation, and return a type without X |
| A template dependency with `scope="RUNTIME"` | `Cannot access built-in declaration 'kotlin.Any'`, or an unresolved class of the `.shared` module | Change the scope of `kotlin-stdlib` or of the `.shared` module to compile |
| A class hierarchy that needs a platform dependency | `cannot access BaseClass: class file not found` | Keep the platform dependency, also without direct imports |
| A large move | Many modules fail to compile | After you move 10 or more files, build `//plugins/... //contrib/...` |
| A nullable override after a Java to Kotlin conversion | `'override' overrides nothing` | Match the parameter types of the base class |
| A Kotlin interface constant used from Java | `cannot find symbol CONSTANT_NAME` | Write `MyInterface.CONSTANT_NAME` |
| A top-level Kotlin function used from Java | `cannot find symbol myFunction` | Import it from `MyFileKt` |
| `object : JavaInterface()` | `This type does not have a constructor` | Remove the parentheses |

## Examples

- `intellij.javascript.regexp` (Pattern A): `JSRegexpInjector`, `JSRegexpHost` and `JSRegExpModifierProvider` moved out of `javascript-backend`.
- `intellij.javascript.backend.css` (Pattern B): the `JsCssIntegrationHelper` extension point in `javascript-backend`. The users in `javascript-ultimate`, `jsf-core` and `webpack` needed fixes.
- `intellij.javascript.backend.spellchecker` (Pattern A): CoffeeScript subclasses `JSSpellcheckingStrategy`, so the module is `public`, and the class and its inner tokenizer are `open`.
- `intellij.javascript.backend.xml` (Pattern A and B): about 40 files moved, and the `JsXmlContextHelper` extension point replaced the `XmlTag` checks in about 60 files.
- `intellij.vuejs.backend.css` (Pattern B, three extension points): `VueCssExtractHelper` passes a `List<CssSelectorSuffix>` as `Any?` state. `VueCssLanguageProvider` returns `Language`, not `PostCssLanguage`, to stop a supertype chain.
